active_risks.text: US-Iran Hormuz blockade: extended US port blockade threatens prolonged oil supply disruption, with WTI rebounding to $81 on renewed tensions.
US-China semiconductor supply-chain decoupling: China's domestic DUV scanner and CXMT listing pressure memory and equipment names, while US trade sanctions escalate.

geopolitical.market_impact: Oil's wobbly de-escalation premium keeps energy costs elevated, benefiting defense contractor PLTR and power-infra names like BE, while squeezing hyperscaler capex margins (AMZN, MSFT). The memory supply-chain threat from China is fully priced in the recent drawdown, but the repricing rally shows the cycle's resilience. Rates at cycle highs cap Big Tech valuations and make the NVDA/AMD demand story focused on execution, not multiple expansion.
geopolitical.new_since_yesterday: Taiwan's TSMC reportedly developing advanced packaging resembling Intel's EMIB, adding competitive risk to Intel's foundry thesis (per Simply Wall St., Aug 4).

base.description: Hormuz stalemate persists with WTI oscillating $80-85; Fed holds in September, but rising energy costs keep core CPI sticky. optimistic.description: Ceasefire agreement reached, WTI drops to $70-75; disinflation returns, Fed cuts in September. Hyperscalers ease memory cost pressures, margins expand. Semis break out, led by NVDA and MU, and Singapore banks surge as rates fall. The 'AI trade is back on' narrative lifts all boats.

pessimistic.description: Hormuz blockade intensifies, WTI spikes to $95-100; US-Iran military escalation drives a flight to safety. Fed forced to hike 25bp in Sep, crushing Big Tech and capex-heavy names. Samsung and SK Hynix miss on memory demand, and the CXMT overhang turns into a genuine supply glut, sending semis down 15-20%.

wildcard.description: A US-China trade deal: China removes export controls on rare earths and Ga/Ge in exchange for NVIDIA H200 export licenses. The semiconductor supply chain reopens, sending equipment makers like ASML up 20% in a week and memory stocks rocketing as oversupply fears evaporate.
